deadline.value: PhD applicants (domestic and international) must submit everything by December 1, 2026; this is a hard deadline.
deadline.quote: Ph.D. applicants: Domestic and international applicants must have submitted all required materials. | The application date listed for the Ph.D. program is a hard deadline.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

toefl_min.value: Competitive international applicants score at least 92 on the TOEFL iBT (and rank in the top 5% of a respected ChemE program).
toefl_min.quote: To be competitive, such applicants must be highly ranked (top 5%) in a respected chemical engineering program, show evidence of the ability to carry out independent research and score at least 92 (internet-based) on the TOEFL.

supervisor.value: Don't ask faculty to pre-review you; a committee admits you and forwards your file to faculty in your area.
supervisor.quote: Please do not ask a faculty member to review your qualifications before applying. | the committee forwards your application to the appropriate person(s), who will then contact you

funding.value: Nearly all admitted PhD students receive tuition, health insurance and a stipend.
funding.quote: Nearly all admitted Ph.D. candidates receive financial support, which includes tuition, health insurance and a competitive stipend.

entry_route.value: Bachelor's graduates in ChemE or related fields can apply; applicants with an MS from elsewhere are also considered.
entry_route.quote: We have admitted some students whose undergraduate degrees are in related engineering or science fields | students who have obtained a graduate (e.g., M.S.) degree elsewhere, or have substantial industrial experience can be considered for the Ph.D.

notes: Apply to both the Graduate School and the department. Off-quarter entry needs a year of graduate ChemE coursework.
